title: Free tutorial: Write a YARA rule for a lure
summary: Write a YARA rule that catches a phishing lure and nothing else, and test it on every file.

next.title: Seminar 3: SOC triage: alerts, phishing, threat intel and AI verdicts

script.intro: Welcome. A YARA rule describes what a file looks like. In this tutorial you write one that catches a phishing lure and nothing else.
script.outro: Tight rules are trusted rules. Seminar 3 puts this next to alert triage, threat intelligence and checking an AI's verdicts.
steps: Read the setting so you know the company, the date and the time zone. Then open the evidence in the case folder.

The first rule matches on the lure's domain alone. Run it against every file in the case and see what else it catches: the threat-intel feed and the proxy log mention that domain too, so it is too loose. A rule for email should need things only the email has: the subject line, the link path and the threat wording. Add all three as strings, require all of them in the condition, and test again. One match, on the right file, is the goal. A rule that fires on the wrong file wastes an analyst's night.
Tight rules are trusted rules. Seminar 3 puts this next to alert triage, threat intelligence and checking an AI's verdicts.
